newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain CEOE says will be tough to reach labour deal.
newsitem.headline: Spain CEOE says will be tough to reach labour deal.

text.p: Spanish employers' association (CEOE) president Jose Maria Cuevas said on Tuesday that he saw no way to agree a reform of some dismissal rules and that it would require a maximum effort to reach an overall deal.

Unions and employers enter final talks to reform Spain's rigid labour market rules later on Tuesday, and the conservative Popular Party government has said it would step in if the two fail to reach a deal soon.
"We still don't know how to reach a deal on some dismissals," Cuevas told journalists.
Cuevas added that employers accepted trade union demands that severance for unfair dismissal be maintained at 45 days.

The CEOE insists, however, that legitimate dismissal costs should be reduced to 20 days for each year worked with a maximum outlay of 12 months salary from current uncertain, but typically higher payments.
Cuevas said it would need a maximum effort in this latest part of talks to bring employers and trade unions closer together.
